_documentation.purpose: Geometry test prompts for the PDSF (Predictive-Discursive-Stylistic-Framework) decomposition experiment (SpecA).
_documentation.overview: 224 prompts organized as 14 groups × 16 variants. Each group asks a simple factual or logical question with a known single-token answer (Yes, No, True, A, or B). The 16 variants per group are generated by a 2^4 full factorial design that systematically varies 4 surface-form factors while holding the semantic content (question + answer) constant.
_documentation.experimental_logic: By holding the answer constant and varying only surface form, we can cleanly separate the model's internal representations into: (1) P (Predictive) — the direction used for prediction (should be identical across variants), (2) D (Discursive) — directions that differ between variants (captures surface-form effects), and (3) S (Stylistic) — directions shared within a group that encode 'which question is being asked'. The factorial design enables Part C to measure the causal effect of each factor on D-space energy.

factorial_design.A_paraphrase: Two different wordings of the same question. A=0: 'Is X equal to Y?', A=1: 'Does X equal Y?' (varies by group).
factorial_design.B_constraint: Whether an explicit answer-constraint phrase is included. B=0: none, B=1: 'Answer using the allowed word only.'
factorial_design.C_clutter: Whether a preamble/context sentence is prepended. C=0: none, C=1: 'This is a simple arithmetic check.' (varies by domain).
factorial_design.D_format: Style of the output instruction. D=0: terse imperative ('Output exactly one word. Do not explain.'), D=1: verbose declarative ('Your response should be a single word from the following options...').

_documentation.variant_id_encoding: Each variant_id ends with a suffix like A0B0C1D0, encoding the factor levels. A0B0C0D0 is the 'bare' prompt (no constraint, no clutter, terse format, version 1). A1B1C1D1 has all four factors active.

group_structure.domains: arith (arithmetic), logic (propositional logic), fact (factual knowledge), ling (linguistics)

how_the_pipeline_uses_this.cell_15: Parses groups and variants into flat lists (prompts, group_ids, variant_ids, expected_tokens, meta).
how_the_pipeline_uses_this.meta_rows: Each variant's A, B, C, D values are splatted into meta via **{k:v ...}, so meta[i]['A'] = 0 or 1.
how_the_pipeline_uses_this.part_c: compute_part_C_factor_effects() reads meta_rows[i].get('A'), .get('B'), etc. to split prompts by factor level.
how_the_pipeline_uses_this.P_basis: expected_next_token is used to look up unembedding vectors for the P (predictive) subspace.
how_the_pipeline_uses_this.group_ids: Used by Parts B, E, H to define within-group vs between-group comparisons.

fixes_applied.description: Added actual paraphrase variation (Factor A) to N03, N05, N07 groups which previously had identical A0/A1 prompts
